items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I read the other day about Sam Goody and Korvette's, that some of these albums, they are bootleg from tapes and they put them out and they make that money.

ctx.x: We'll talk about that air check, that was one that was released on the Pumpkin label. I suppose it's a bootleg of some sort even though it does have liner notes and most bootlegs don't have liner notes, you certainly didn't know anything about it being released.

Yes, I called the Union, trying to see if we could get some money out of this down there in Florida, but couldn't do anything about it. It happened so long ago and unless we had a contract with him or had some kind of an agreement, they couldn't do anything, couldn't hurt him any. So like the record business now, it's all bootleg, they call it, you know. I read the other day about Sam Goody and Korvette's, that some of these albums, they are bootleg from tapes and they put them out and they make that money. So…
That's right. And it was recorded -- Boston 1951.
